misconceptions.description: Treating the finished lesson plan or screenshot as the portfolio evidence, without the reasoning and outcome that make it claim-worthy
misconceptions.trigger: entry includes a polished artifact but no claim, standard, or result it is meant to demonstrate
misconceptions.feedback: An artifact becomes evidence only when paired with the claim it supports and the outcome it produced. Attach the reasoning.

misconceptions.description: Asserting that a competency was met without pointing to the specific part of the artifact that shows it
misconceptions.trigger: reflection claims a standard was demonstrated but cites no concrete location or moment in the evidence
misconceptions.feedback: Point to the exact line, decision, or student-work moment that warrants the claim. A claim with no warrant is an assertion.

misconceptions.description: Stretching one artifact to claim it demonstrates many unrelated standards at once
misconceptions.trigger: a single lesson plan is tagged to five competencies it does not all evidence
misconceptions.feedback: Match each claim to the artifact that genuinely shows it. Overclaiming weakens the entries that are real.

misconceptions.description: Treating the polished quality of an AI-assisted artifact as evidence of the competency, when polish is exactly what a tool can fabricate.
misconceptions.trigger: portfolio entry leans on artifact quality rather than an inspectable warrant and a measured outcome
misconceptions.feedback: Foreground what a tool cannot fabricate: the warrant linking the artifact to the standard and the measured outcome it produced. A beautiful artifact with no inspectable reasoning is weaker evidence than a rough one with a verifiable warrant.
